data.name: Body
data.gender_notes: Body is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, the word ‘Body’ refers to the physical form of an individual. However, in a Christian context, ‘Body’ is more than just a physical form. It is the temple of the Holy Spirit, a vessel for God's love and grace. As the Apostle Paul wrote in 1 Corinthians 6:19–20: ‘Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore honor God with your bodies.’
data.spiritual_meaning: Vessel for God's love and grace
data.etymology: Body belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Temple of the Holy Spirit.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Body total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.long_meaning: The Hebrew word for body is derived from the word 'boded', which means 'your work'. In a biblical context, it can refer to the physical body as the work of God, or to the body as the vessel for the soul.

in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek word for body is 'soma'. It is used extensively in the New Testament to refer to the physical body, as well as to the body of Christ and the body of the church.

in_latin.name: corpus
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin word for body is 'corpus'. It is used in various religious and philosophical contexts, including in the Latin Vulgate Bible and in Catholic theology.

in_english.name: Body
in_english.long_meaning: In English, the word 'body' refers to a physical organism, as well as to a group or collection of things. In a biblical context, it can refer to the physical body as the temple of the Holy Spirit or as the vessel for the soul.

data.cultural_impact: In Western culture, the phrase "give your body a rest" or "listen to your body" has become commonplace, emphasizing the importance of physical health and wellness. In the Christian faith, the body holds a deeper meaning. It is considered a sacred gift from God and the vessel through which we experience the world and connect with others and ultimately with God.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian faith, the body is not just a physical form but a temple of the Holy Spirit. Christians believe that God dwells in them through the Holy Spirit, and therefore, they must care for and honor their bodies as sacred vessels. This not only includes taking care of physical health but also nurturing the mind, heart, and soul. By living a virtuous and holy life, Christians demonstrate their reverence for God and seek to align their bodies with the will of God. Ultimately, the body is a reminder of the physical and spiritual wholeness that believers have been given as a gift from God.
